scope: Ten selected references supporting narrative comparisons; not an exhaustive novelty audit. Preprints and repository drafts are identified explicitly.

references.title: Computing Partitions with Applications to the Knapsack Problem
references.role: Foundational meet-in-the-middle time bound; an author-hosted copy supplies primary evidence.

references.title: A T=O(2^{n/2}), S=O(2^{n/4}) Algorithm for Certain NP-Complete Problems
references.role: Foundational time-space tradeoff; publisher abstract and bibliographic record.

references.title: Sums of Lexicographically Ordered Sets
references.role: The institutional abstract establishes ordered distinct sums with efficient decision; no equivalence to the overlap-product theorem is asserted.

references.title: Subset Sum via Partial Match
references.role: Recent randomized worst-case improvement via compatibility testing; distinct from the deterministic structural guarantee.

references.title: A Near-Linear Pseudopolynomial Time Algorithm for Subset Sum
references.role: Near-linear randomized pseudopolynomial time illustrates the distinction between target magnitude and binary encoding length.

references.title: Beating Bellman's Algorithm for Subset Sum
references.role: Theorem 1.1 computes truncated support in randomized time soft-O(output size times sqrt(n)); contrasts global output sensitivity with small local dictionaries.

references.title: On Near-Linear-Time Algorithms for Dense Subset Sum
references.role: Dense-regime algorithms and conditional lower bounds; not a characterization by the overlap product.

references.title: Parameterized Algorithms on Integer Sets with Small Doubling: Integer Programming, Subset Sum and k-SUM
references.role: Algorithms parameterized by additive doubling; the polynomial exponent can depend on that parameter, unlike a generic fixed-exponent FPT claim.

references.title: A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum
references.venue: Preprint dated September 26, 2026; repository release October 6, 2026
references.role: Recent worst-case time-space work with an explicit word model and randomized construction; cited for comparison, not as a proof of the block-overlap result.

references.title: How Far from Easy? Structural Distance in Subset Sum
references.role: Repository maximum-superincreasing-core construction and exception-count bound, used for the explicit decimal-family comparison.
